rationale: Greek loanword προδότης. Standard NT term applied to Judas. Lycopolitan -ⲁⲟ- for -ⲟⲇⲟ-.
Greek loanword διώκτης. Pauline self-description (1 Tim 1:13). Lycopolitan ⲛⲁⲱⲕ- for διωκ-.

Greek loanword ὅραμα 'vision, sight, that-which-is-seen.' Used here as synonym/equivalent of ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲃⲟⲗⲏ — the parable functions as a vision granted to be interpreted. Plural with ⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'two' = the twin parable of the two trees.
From ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined, be agreed.' The 'agreement' or 'harmony' of some power by which the molded ones are fashioned. Distinct from ⲧⲱⲧ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'persuasion/conviction.'
Lycopolitan rendering of ⲓⲟⲩⲇⲁⲥ. The Iscariot, paired in this passage with Paul as inverse biographical types.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'the Lord.' Vowel-shift ⲟⲉⲓ → ⲁⲓ̈ and ⲭ for palatal. Used here for the Christian church 'of the Lord.'

Possibly = ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ 'manifestation' or a botanical term for branch/shoot. Used in the typological identification 'X are the manifestation of the beautiful tree.' Confidence low pending parallels in following pages.
